channel.title: Sofa Updates
channel.description: Signed, notarized Sofa releases for Apple silicon Macs.

item.description:
Sofa — Your TV, from your Mac.
Sofa 1.0.0 is the first stable release. Build 16 improves discovery and keeps your TV pairing when its network address changes. Android/Google TV and Samsung Tizen adapters remain experimental.
### Find your TV again automatically - Remember the paired TV’s stable identity and approved certificate, with credentials retained in their original Keychain item. - Rediscover a known TV after its IP address changes and reconnect without a new pairing code when its identity and certificate match. - Search more VIDAA, Android/Google TV and Samsung announcements, verify remote services, and retry after connection loss, network changes and Mac wake. - Keep explicit recovery guidance for denied Local Network permission, missing remote services and certificate changes.
### Installation and updates Download the **DMG**, drag Sofa to Applications, then open it normally. Requires Apple silicon and macOS 26 or later. Existing build 15 users receive this release through Sofa’s signed automatic update feed; earlier builds need one manual DMG installation. Saved TV pairings are preserved.
The ZIP is the automatic-update package. Use the DMG for normal manual installation. SHA-256 checksums accompany both files.
### Validation and compatibility - Apple notarization accepted. Developer ID signed, with the notarization ticket stapled. The app inside both the DMG and updater ZIP passes Gatekeeper assessment. - 73 Python tests and Swift state checks passed, including protocol, TLS, identity migration, persistence and discovery cancellation tests. - On the development Hisense VIDAA TV, Sofa recovered from a deliberately stale saved address and reconnected without a new pairing code. The same pairing identity, certificate and Keychain account were retained. This was a saved-address simulation, not a router DHCP lease change. - VIDAA is physically tested on one Hisense A4K-series TV. Other models and firmware need wider testing. Android/Google TV and Samsung have automated coverage but no physical-device verification yet. - Sleeping TVs, denied permissions, blocked multicast and network isolation can prevent discovery. Android devices need Android TV Remote Service v2. Samsung needs secure remote control; older Orsay TVs are unsupported. Volume sliders appear only with compatible feedback.
Free and open source under the MIT license. No Sofa account or analytics.

item.title: 0.6.0-beta.1
item.description:
Sofa — Your TV, from your Mac.
This beta adds native automatic updates and the new Lounge Remote icon. **Build 15 is Apple notarized**, Developer ID signed by TOP NOTCH COMPANY LIMITED, and distributed with its notarization ticket stapled.
### Updates that stay out of the way - Daily background checks and automatic downloads, with installation when Sofa quits. - Settings → Updates to control automatic behavior; Check for Updates in Sofa's menu and Settings for an immediate check or installation and relaunch. - Gentle reminders inside the menu-bar panel instead of interrupting your TV session. - Signed update feeds and packages, verified before extraction. Only notarized releases enter the public update feed. - Existing bundle and Keychain identities are preserved, so saved TV pairing carries forward.
### Refreshed identity - Native Lounge Remote app icon with a unified remote body and subtle sofa-seat detail. - Matching outline-only menu-bar icon and “Your TV, from your Mac.” branding.
### Installation Download the **DMG**, open it, drag Sofa to Applications, then open Sofa normally. Apple silicon and macOS 26 or later are required. Existing build 13/14 users need this one manual upgrade to gain automatic updates. The ZIP is also supplied for the updater and users who prefer an archive.
### Validation and limits - Apple notarization, staple validation and Gatekeeper acceptance passed for the app extracted from the ZIP and mounted from the DMG. - All 60 Python tests and Swift state checks passed. - The actual app in an isolated test identity rejected a corrupted update without replacing itself, installed a valid signed update and relaunched, and downloaded another update silently and installed it on normal Quit. These local test packages were signed, not separately notarized. - The public updater's first release is build 15; a later production build will be needed to verify a public-to-public upgrade. - VIDAA support is tested with the development TV. Google / Android TV and Samsung Tizen remain experimental and have not been verified with physical hardware. Volume sliders appear only when supported feedback is available. Older Samsung Orsay models are not supported.
Free and open source under the MIT license. No Sofa account or analytics. See docs/PRIVACY.md for update download metadata and settings.
